Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing — follow-up and next steps

Hi Jamie / Carlos,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — appreciate the time. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size Dedicated capacity properly:

Call recap (high level):
- Deployment preference: Dedicated capacity (customer-managed VPC) — may evaluate Private/on‑prem later for regulated workloads.
- Workload profile (what you mentioned on the call): peak TPS around ~140, sustained TPS ~40–50, concurrency spikes up to ~30 during morning window.
- Token mix: ~500 prompt tokens avg, ~1,000 completion tokens avg (rough mix 1:2).
- Primary model family: experimenting with 13B quantized variants initially, potential ramp to larger 30–70B models for specific customers.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you share the demand forecast spreadsheet you mentioned (daily/hourly traffic, expected ramp, and any burst windows)? that will let us map TPS -> GPU footprint.
2) Confirm whether strict VPC-only access is required (yes/no) and any egress/KMS requirements.
3) Would you like us to default-sizing for A100(80GB) nodes or evaluate H100/A2 alternatives? (we'll propose options with cost + throughput tradeoffs).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- I'll review the forecast and put together two sizing options (conservative and optimized) with estimated throughput and cost.
- Schedule a 30–45m technical deep-dive with your infra lead (Carlos) + our solutions engineer to walk model + quantization tradeoffs and network requirements.
- Rafael will follow up on pricing/SLA and procurement flow.

If you can drop the forecast and procurement contact here I’ll get the sizing draft out by end-of-day Thursday.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Perfect — thanks for the file, Jamie. I reviewed the hourly profile and put together an initial sizing recommendation and assumptions below. This is a starting point; we'll validate in the tech deep-dive and during a short POC.

Assumptions:
- Model family: 13B quantized for initial estimates. Larger models will materially increase GPU RAM and latency tradeoffs.
- Token mix: prompt ~520 / completion ~980.
- Target SLOs: p95 latency target ~750ms for 1k token responses (we'll tune batching/tracing in the POC).

Initial sizing options (ballpark):
1) Optimized (cost-efficient): 4x A100 80GB GPUs (single cluster) — expected to handle sustained ~45 TPS with burst headroom to ~120 TPS with autoscaling and aggressive batching/prefix cache. Good fit if most traffic uses 13B quantized models.
2) Conservative (performance-first): 6x A100 80GB GPUs (single cluster) — more headroom for concurrency spikes and smoother p95 during bursts; recommended if you plan to enable larger 30–70B models soon.

Notes on GPU type: A100(80GB) is a good default for quantized 13B/30B workflows. If you plan to run 70B models regularly, we should evaluate H100 or more distributed sharding (or Redwood Private with co-located infra). We'll cover tradeoffs in the deep-dive.

Next steps I suggest:
- Tech deep-dive (30–45m) — propose Wed 2026-03-10 10:00–10:45am PT. Carlos + your ML/infra person + our solutions engineer + inference engineer.
- Rafael will share preliminary SLA/pricing and a draft commitment footprint based on the final sizing option you pick.
- Short POC (2–4 weeks) to validate latency and autoscaling under your peak profile.

Do any of the above options look reasonable? If so I’ll lock the deep-dive and Rafael will start the procurement thread.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
